selection: step-out from bonsai1/L2/N6893- (10x queue, model pilot: haiku)

neighbours.label: ' quite' as a degree intensifier before an adjective or noun
fire: The new software update is quite confusing for older users.
Honestly, the cafeteria lunch was quite good.
The lake looked quite different at dawn after the flood.
It was quite a long walk to the station.
Her answer seemed quite reasonable to the committee.
The paint dries quite slowly in cold rooms.
We were quite sure the bus had already left.
He is quite tall for his age.
quiet: Older users find the new software update confusing.
Surprisingly, the cafeteria lunch turned out decent.
Once the storm passed, the lake looked different at dawn.
That walk to the station took a long time.
Her answer made sense to the committee members.
Paint takes a long time to dry in cold rooms.
We were certain the bus had already left.
He is tall for his age, yet still a child.

notes: Model pilot (haiku arm; the same pole is tested independently by the other arm, pairing disclosed): this pole feeds the held pole bonsai1/L2/N6893- (zeroing this neuron removes 0.86 of the anchor's peak), from a batched edge measurement with 8 same-layer placebos. Label and all 16 sentences written by the Haiku 5.5 labeller from a packet (card + all-pole band samples + the edge hint) and one probe round of 8 sentences (none reused). An Opus gate checked rule-level items only and edited nothing. Labeller's note: All four probe fire sentences scored 0.80 to 0.94 and all four same-frame near misses stayed under 0.01, including 'very' and 'still' as controls, so the token and its degree sense hold. Band samples also show ' quite' in degree uses, so the sense is consistent; the test is the bare word in a degree slot, not the only sense of quite, which I did not probe.
